conviction_note: The Q4 revenue bar ($7.1-7.3m, the guide midpoint) looks beatable given management's May call commentary, and the FY27 guide faces headwinds management has already disclosed (aerospace pullback, cystoscope partial insourcing, tariff credit memos). On a name whose last four prints show record-revenue beats buying -0.9%, -10.4%, -0.6% and +3.9%, the fundamental lean of about +6% on revenue translates to a near-zero reaction, so +0.2 is the sum of three small findings and not a call.
bar: Q4 FY26 revenue $7.1-7.3m: company FY26 guide $29-31m less nine-month $22.8m gives $6.2-8.2m, midpoint $7.2m (https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/05/13/3294465/34800/en/Precision-Optics-Reports-Third-Quarter-Fiscal-Year-2026-Financial-Results.html). Two estimate sources roughly agree: Quiver Quantitative $7.29m (https://www.quiverquant.com/news/PRECISION+OPTICS+Q4+2026+Earnings+Preview:+Recent+$POCI+Insider+Trading,+Hedge+Fund+Activity,+and+More) and MarketBeat-syndicated $7.10m with EPS -$0.06 (https://www.defenseworld.net/2026/09/17/precision-optics-poci-to-announce-quarterly-earnings-on-thursday.html). Implied Q4 adj. EBITDA from the FY guide is -$0.1m to -$0.3m (nine months -$2.4m), and the CFO said 'roughly breakeven'. One analyst covers the name, rated Hold with a $4 target (TipRanks).
positioning_check: Short interest is about 0.1% of shares, 10,912 shares at the 2026-08-31 settlement, 0.3 days to cover (https://www.dailypolitical.com/2026/09/16/precision-optics-corp-nasdaqpoci-sees-large-drop-in-short-interest.html, via the sweep row). There is no options market, so there is no skew. Run-up is +6.85% over 5 days and +8.07% over 20 days, following the 09-10 and 09-17 order PRs. The stock is 20% below its 52-week high. With no crowded short, there is no squeeze mechanism on the one negative finding.

findings.finding: The Q4 revenue consensus of $7.1-7.3m equals the mechanical guide midpoint. It implies a 17% sequential drop from Q3's $8.7m ($8.3m net of tariff pass-through), yet the CEO said on the May call that the aerospace ($3.6m) and cystoscopy ($2.2m) lines would 'continue at similar levels that we saw in Q3'. Ross Optical (+65%) was called sustainable and the $3.5m ophthalmic order ships over 12-15 months from May, so underlying Q4 is about $8m or more. The main thing that could close the gap is tariff-refund credit memos, which the CFO said 'reduce sales at the time those credit memos are issued'. Their timing (Q4 or Q1 FY27) is not disclosed.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Every FY26 print was a record-revenue beat or raise, and the stock reacted as follows (close before to close after, from Yahoo daily bars). Q4 FY25 (2025-09-29): 4.39 to 4.35, -0.9%. Q1 FY26 (2025-11-13): 4.83 to 4.33, -10.4%, on 14.2% gross margin. Q2 FY26 (2026-02-17): 4.66 to 4.63, -0.6%. Q3 FY26 (2026-05-13): 4.60 to 4.78, +3.9%, on the first positive adj. EBITDA. So revenue beats have not paid; margins and EBITDA have. findings.why_not_priced: Both published estimates sit at the guide midpoint to within $0.1m, which is what a model that just copies the guide produces. If the market held the call commentary instead, estimates would sit near the $8.2m top of the guide and the stock would have re-rated after May. It has not: it closed $4.78 on 2026-05-14 and $4.755 at the seal. The only analyst is a Hold with a $4 target.
findings.independence: The company's own pattern points the same way: FY26 revenue guidance went from 'in excess of $25m' (2025-09-29, https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2025/09/29/3158150/34800/en/Precision-Optics-Reports-Fourth-Quarter-and-Fiscal-Year-2025-Financial-Results.html) to $26-28m (Feb 2026) to $29-31m (May 2026). The same transcript's tariff credit-memo remark is the offset, and it is already netted into the size.

findings.finding: On 2026-09-21, a week before the release, the board granted the CEO, CFO and COO identical fully vested stock bonuses of 6,742 shares each (Form 4s filed 2026-09-24). Nothing of this form appears in the Aug-Dec 2025 filing record around the FY25 results, which suggests FY26 bonus criteria were judged met with full-year numbers in hand.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior instance. Insider Form 4s on this name have not been associated with a measured reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: A $31k-per-head stock bonus on a $193k/day nano-cap is not carried by any wire or preview. If it were read as a signal, it would show up in the tape as volume after 09-24, which the 20-day average of about 40k shares does not show. It is also plausibly just cash conservation, which is why the size is tiny.
findings.independence: Separate filings from the same event: CFO (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000867840/000168316826007391/ownership.xml) and COO (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000867840/000168316826007390/ownership.xml). These are one fact, counted once.

findings.finding: The FY27 guide, likely issued with this release as the FY26 guide was with the FY25 release, carries three headwinds management disclosed in May. The largest aerospace program (about $3.6m a quarter) faces a 15-20% pullback in Q1-Q2 FY27, the current half. The cystoscope customer will run its own line ('1 shift, maybe 1.5 shifts'), paying POCI a royalty instead of product revenue. Tariff-refund credit memos reduce reported sales. Together these point to a sharp deceleration from +55% growth.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The initial FY26 guide ('in excess of $25m', +31%, with +$0.5m adj. EBITDA) bought -0.9% on 2025-09-30. The Q1 FY26 margin disappointment cost -10.4%, the one large move in the record, so the downside tail on this line is real.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. All three headwinds were said on the public call, and the stock has gone nowhere since May, which is what a market already discounting deceleration looks like. What remains unpriced is only the magnitude. Offsets named in the same call cap it: 5-6 development programs to production in FY27, the ophthalmic order, Ross, and the new satellite and defense orders of 09-10 and 09-17.
findings.independence: Same transcript as finding 1, a different passage and a different line (guide versus quarter). The aerospace pullback is corroborated by the deltasheets Q3 summary (https://deltasheets.substack.com/p/poci-fy2026-q3). The findings do not contradict each other: the quarter can beat while the guide decelerates.

baseline_tension: The baseline has no options, no skew and an empty history. The modest +8% 20-day run-up leans the same way as the small positive quarter read, so what I found largely agrees with the price, and the net number is correspondingly near zero.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (reaction function has veto): the Q4 revenue-beat finding went from +1.0 to +0.5, because this name's record-revenue prints bought -0.9, -10.4, -0.6 and +3.9 and it trades on margin and EBITDA, not revenue.
Lesson 5 (documents beat inference): the stock-bonus Form 4 finding went from +0.3 to +0.2, because the document is primary but its meaning (bonus criteria met) is inference.

Lesson 3 (own caveat reaches the number): the FY27-guide headwind finding went from -1.0 to -0.5, because its own why_not_priced says all three headwinds were disclosed on the public call and the stock has been flat since.
Lesson 6 (verify the bar): the bar sources to the company guide and two roughly agreeing estimates, so no cap was applied; all findings resolve 2026-09-29, inside the window.
Lesson 8 (thin coverage) was considered and not applied: finding 1 is inference from call commentary, not a confirmed number, so it does not qualify for upsizing.
